prompts.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: photographic exercise demonstration sprite sheet for the ATLAS fitness app, a draft for human review.
Primary request: create a single horizontal three-panel storyboard of an adult athlete performing a goblet squat, left-to-right chronological phases. The final canvas should have aspect ratio exactly 3:1, ideally 3072 by 1024 pixels, comprising THREE equally wide square panels. No gutters, frames, text, numbers, arrows, logos, watermarks, or decorative elements.
Scene/backdrop: neutral dark navy-gray seamless studio wall and matte gray floor; identical soft side lighting in all panels.
Subject: same adult woman with an athletic but natural build, short tied-back dark hair, wearing a plain muted navy short-sleeve athletic shirt, gray full-length athletic pants, and white flat training shoes. Hold ONE compact black dumbbell vertically close to the chest, both hands cupping its upper head. Realistic skin, fabric, and equipment textures.
Camera/composition: fixed three-quarter side view at waist height, full body from head to shoes always visible with generous margins, same model scale and foot positions in all three panels. Each panel is the SAME locked camera and studio frame at a different instant; align the floor/horizon exactly.
Frame 1 LEFT: standing tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes slightly outward, dumbbell at chest.
Frame 2 MIDDLE: halfway down into the squat, knees bending in line with toes, hips lowering, heels planted and chest upright.
Frame 3 RIGHT: controlled bottom of squat, thighs approximately parallel to floor, neutral spine, heels planted, knees follow toes, dumbbell remains close to chest.
Constraints: plausible human anatomy, two arms and two legs only, natural joints, no exaggerated muscles, no twisted hands; same person/clothing/dumbbell/lighting/camera across all panels. Keep the three stages visually distinct. Photorealistic premium fitness editorial photography, precise and restrained. Do not depict injury or strain.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: photographic exercise demonstration sprite sheet for the ATLAS fitness app, a draft for human review.
Primary request: create a single horizontal three-panel storyboard of an adult athlete performing a standard bodyweight push-up, left-to-right chronological phases. Canvas aspect ratio exactly 3:1, ideally 3072 by 1024 pixels, comprising THREE equally wide square panels. No gutters, frames, text, numbers, arrows, logos, watermarks, or decorative elements.
Scene/backdrop: neutral dark navy-gray seamless studio wall and matte gray floor; identical soft side lighting in all panels.
Subject: same adult man with a natural athletic build and short dark hair, wearing a plain muted navy short-sleeve athletic shirt, gray athletic shorts and white training shoes. Realistic skin and fabric texture.
Camera/composition: completely fixed side view from slightly above floor height, body horizontal across each square frame with full head-to-shoes and both hands visible, generous margins, identical scale and same hands and toe positions in all three panels. All panels are the same locked camera frame at different moments. Align floor/horizon exactly.
Frame 1 LEFT: high plank at the top of a push-up, palms on floor slightly wider than shoulders and under shoulder line, arms extended without hyperextension, body forms a straight line from head through hips to heels, legs straight with toes grounded.
Frame 2 MIDDLE: halfway lowering, elbows bend backwards about 30 to 45 degrees from torso, whole body descends as a rigid unit, head neutral, hips neither sag nor lift.
Frame 3 RIGHT: controlled bottom, chest close to but not resting on floor, elbows approximately 90 degrees, body remains straight head-to-heels, hands and toes fixed in the same positions.
Constraints: plausible anatomy; only two arms, two hands and two legs; natural joints and fingers; identical model, clothes, lighting, camera and limb lengths in every panel. Keep poses visually distinct. Premium photorealistic fitness editorial photography. Do not depict knees on floor or a hip sag.
prompts.repairPrompt: Edit this push-up three-panel exercise sprite sheet. Keep the 3:1 canvas, three equal square panels, exact same man, clothing, navy-gray studio, camera, floor, light, and the left and middle panels unchanged. Correct ONLY the man's pose in the RIGHT panel: he must be at the bottom of a proper push-up with his chest slightly above the floor and a rigid straight line from shoulders through hips to heels. Raise his pelvis and thighs away from the floor so his hips and knees DO NOT sag or touch the ground. Keep hands and toes grounded, elbows bent approximately 90 degrees, head neutral aligned with spine. Preserve the same hand/toe locations and realistic body proportions. No text, numbers, arrows, borders, watermark or additional objects. Photorealistic.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: photographic exercise demonstration sprite sheet for the ATLAS fitness app, a draft for human review.
Primary request: create a single horizontal three-panel storyboard of an adult athlete performing a stationary bodyweight split squat, left-to-right chronological phases. Canvas aspect ratio exactly 3:1, ideally 3072 by 1024 pixels, comprising THREE equally wide square panels. No gutters, frames, text, numbers, arrows, logos, watermarks or decorative elements.
Scene/backdrop: neutral dark navy-gray seamless studio wall and matte gray floor; identical soft side lighting in all panels.
Subject: same adult woman with a natural athletic build and tied-back dark hair, wearing a plain muted navy short-sleeve athletic shirt, gray full-length athletic pants, white flat training shoes. No weights or other equipment. Hands resting comfortably on hips. Realistic skin and fabric texture.
Camera/composition: fixed SIDE view at waist height, facing right, full head-to-shoes visible with generous margins; same body scale, SAME fixed front foot and back toe contact positions across all three frames; align studio floor/horizon exactly. One foot steps forward roughly a comfortable stride length, front foot fully planted, rear heel raised, both feet on the floor rather than on a bench. Keep this static split stance throughout.
Frame 1 LEFT: starting upright in a split stance, front leg nearly straight with a soft knee, back leg extended behind on toes, upright relaxed torso.
Frame 2 MIDDLE: halfway lowering the body vertically, both knees bending, front heel planted and rear heel raised; torso remains upright, hands on hips.
Frame 3 RIGHT: bottom of the split squat, front knee bent roughly 90 degrees and tracking over the foot, rear knee bent and hovering slightly above the floor, rear foot supported on toes. Front shin near vertical, torso upright, pelvis level.
Constraints: plausible anatomy, only two arms and two legs, natural joints; same model/face/clothing/lighting/lens/foot placement in every panel. Make the descent phases clearly distinct. This is a stationary split squat, NOT a walking lunge, NOT a Bulgarian split squat, NOT a kneeling pose. Photorealistic premium fitness editorial photography; restrained and precise.
